answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may post offers or earn reputation. If several identities coordinate to fake demand, the protocol can sample their commitments and slash the stake when they violate a signed order or fail to deliver; merely sharing an owner is not proof of fraud. This makes a sybil campaign costly: the attacker must tie up real capital for every identity and risks losing it. A timber seller, a sonnet writer, and a jade trader all face the same rule.
